text:
# Terms of Service — draft

Effective: [EFFECTIVE DATE] · Version: [TERMS VERSION]

SESSION is operated by [LEGAL NAME], [POSTAL ADDRESS] ("SESSION," "we," or "us"). Contact us at [SUPPORT EMAIL]. Once finalized and brought into effect, these Terms will govern your use of SESSION and incorporate the Collaboration Permissions and Copyright Policy below. Our Privacy Notice explains how we handle personal information.

## 1. Joining SESSION

You must be at least 18, reside in the United States, and be legally able to enter this agreement. If you act for a company or group, you must have authority to accept these Terms for it. When these Terms take effect, acceptance will be requested through the account or update flow. No acceptance of this draft is being collected. Simply viewing a public page does not transfer rights in anything you create.

Use accurate account information and protect access to your identity provider. Tell us promptly if someone uses your SESSION account without permission. Do not impersonate another person, misstate professional credentials, or access an account you do not control. Profile roles identify the role a member selects; they are not a verification or endorsement of expertise.

## 2. What the service provides

SESSION helps artists, producers, and engineers discover work, exchange feedback, develop private working versions, and meet in live collaboration rooms. The initial service does not collect payments, sell beat licenses, distribute releases, register copyrights, collect royalties, or settle ownership disputes. A member's offer or promise does not bind SESSION.

Save your own project backups. Features, availability, storage limits, and connection quality may vary. We will provide reasonable advance notice of material service reductions when practicable, including an opportunity to retrieve your content, unless urgent security, legal, or operational circumstances prevent it.

## 3. Your content and permissions

"Content" includes recordings, stems, compositions, lyrics, performances, images, project files, metadata, messages, and other material you provide. As between you and SESSION, you retain the rights you hold in your Content. Uploading a file does not make SESSION its owner.

You grant SESSION a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to store, reproduce, process, transmit, display, and play your Content only as reasonably needed to operate the features you choose, apply your sharing permissions, maintain security, and address support or rights requests. This includes creating technical copies, previews, and compatible playback formats. We may authorize service providers to perform these tasks for us under appropriate obligations. This license does not authorize selling your music, using it in unrelated advertisements, or training general-purpose AI models on it.

The license lasts while you make Content available through the service and afterward only for the limited retention, existing private collaborations, and legal purposes described in these Terms and the Privacy Notice. Removing public access stops new public access and new collaboration grants through SESSION. It cannot recall copies already received by others. Continued use of a previously authorized working version is limited by the Collaboration Permissions below. Nothing here eliminates a privacy right provided by law.

You decide whether to keep a project private, share it with room members, publish it for listening, or enable open collaboration. The permission shown at the time someone creates a working version controls that version. Public availability is not a commercial license. A private setting limits access through SESSION; it cannot prevent an authorized recipient from making a separate copy.

## 4. Rights you must have

Only upload or transmit Content you own or are authorized to use in the way you select. Your permission must cover all relevant components, including the recording, composition, samples, loops, lyrics, artwork, and other people's performances or likenesses. Obtain any collaborator, publisher, label, employer, or other authorization needed for that use. A purchased download, a subscription, a credit line, or a short sample does not by itself establish sufficient permission.

If you rely on a legal exception such as fair use, you are responsible for having a supportable basis. We do not require an uploader to claim that every lawful use needs a license. Keep appropriate evidence of your rights and do not submit false ownership or clearance claims.

## 5. Collaboration and release decisions

Members keep the rights they already hold. A creator credit, project-owner label, room-host role, file timestamp, or percentage entered in a draft is not a determination of copyright ownership. SESSION does not automatically assign publishing shares, master ownership, producer points, work-for-hire status, or payment obligations.

The default open-collaboration permission permits private experimentation only, as detailed below. Commercial distribution, public release of a derivative version, advertising use, sublicensing, and upload to a distributor require separate permission from all people whose authorization is needed. Members should record agreed credits, composition shares, recording ownership, clearances, and release approval in a separate agreement before releasing work.

## 6. Live rooms and messages

Rooms support up to four participants. Enable your microphone or camera only when you want to transmit to the room. Review the people present and the room-sharing selection before sending unreleased work. Leave the room or disable the relevant device to stop your transmission.

Do not record, transcribe, rebroadcast, or stream a room or another person's performance without clear permission from every participant and any additional rightsholder permission required. Agreement to these Terms is not blanket consent to another member's recording. SESSION's initial live-room feature does not itself record room audio or video; text chat and connection information are handled as described in the Privacy Notice. Participants may still use external recording tools, and SESSION cannot guarantee that they will obey these rules.

## 7. Acceptable use

Do not use SESSION to:

- Infringe rights, expose another person's private information, or upload material you lack permission to share.
- Harass, threaten, exploit, deceive, or unlawfully discriminate against people; distribute sexual exploitation material or nonconsensual intimate content.
- Impersonate people, misrepresent a collaboration or endorsement, manipulate credits, or submit knowingly false reports.
- Send spam, malware, or malicious files; bypass access controls; extract private audio; overload the service; or probe others' accounts without authorization.
- Collect members' information for unrelated marketing, surveillance, or model training without an appropriate independent basis and the required permissions.

Security researchers may report concerns privately to [SUPPORT OR SECURITY EMAIL]. These rules do not restrict conduct or reporting that applicable law protects.

## 8. Reports, review, and account action

Report abusive behavior or a safety issue at [ABUSE EMAIL OR REPORT URL]. Use the Copyright Policy for copyright claims. Include the relevant profile, room, project, or file link and enough detail to identify the concern. Do not send unnecessary sensitive information.

We may restrict visibility, remove Content, limit features, or suspend or terminate accounts when reasonably needed to enforce these Terms, protect people or the service, respond to rights complaints, or comply with law. We aim to explain material account action and provide a review route at [REVIEW EMAIL OR FORM], unless doing so would compromise safety, an investigation, or legal obligations. A reviewer will consider relevant context, corrections, and submitted evidence. Copyright counter-notices follow their own process below.

We do not promise to review every file or monitor every room. Permission labels and a file's presence on SESSION do not certify ownership or clearance. Repeat infringement may result in termination under the Copyright Policy.

## 9. Exporting data and deleting content

While signed in, you can export account data as JSON, view your uploaded files, and permanently erase your own uploaded files. Erasing a file removes its hosted content and references across hosted projects that use it. Those projects may remain, but their links to the erased file are removed. Downloaded copies held outside SESSION cannot be recalled.

Deleting a track listing is a separate action from erasing the uploaded file. Removing a listing does not erase its source file or remove that file from other projects. Use the explicit file-erasure control when you want the hosted upload removed. File erasure does not delete your account, all messages, or unrelated project information. Account deletion has not yet been implemented. For other privacy requests, the designated contact will be [PRIVACY EMAIL]. Existing rights and separate agreements between collaborators are not automatically cancelled by removing a file or listing.

## 10. Service responsibilities and limits

To the extent permitted by law, the service is provided as available without warranties that it will always be uninterrupted, error-free, suitable for every workflow, or free from unauthorized member behavior. We remain responsible for duties that the law does not allow us to exclude.

To the extent permitted by law, neither party is liable under these Terms for indirect or consequential loss that was not reasonably foreseeable. SESSION's total liability arising from the service is limited to [APPROVED LIABILITY CAP AND BASIS]. These limits do not apply to fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence where exclusion is prohibited, death or personal injury caused by negligence where applicable, or any liability that cannot lawfully be limited. They do not eliminate your statutory remedies.

## 11. Disputes and governing law

Contact [LEGAL OR SUPPORT EMAIL] with a concern so we can try to resolve it. This does not postpone a legal deadline or prevent either party from seeking urgent relief.

Subject to mandatory law and rights to use a competent local or small-claims court, these Terms are governed by the laws of [STATE], without its conflict-of-laws rules, and disputes may be brought in the competent state or federal courts located in [COUNTY, STATE]. These Terms do not require arbitration or waive class proceedings. The federal-court consent required for a copyright counter-notice is a separate statutory process.

## 12. Changes and other terms

We will post the effective date of revisions and give reasonable notice of material changes through the service or an available account contact. When affirmative agreement is required, we will request it before applying the change. Updated terms do not retroactively authorize a materially different use of previously collected personal information or expand an existing content license without an appropriate basis and any required agreement.

If a provision is unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue where lawful. Failure to enforce a provision once is not a permanent waiver. Neither these Terms nor a collaboration creates employment, an agency relationship, or a partnership with SESSION. You may not transfer your account without our agreement. A lawful transfer of the service remains subject to applicable obligations and the Privacy Notice.

Accessibility assistance is available at [ACCESSIBILITY EMAIL]. Describe the feature and the help you need without including unnecessary private project material.

title: Privacy
text:
# Privacy Notice — draft

Effective: [EFFECTIVE DATE] · Version: [PRIVACY VERSION]

[LEGAL NAME], doing business as SESSION, is responsible for the practices described here. Contact [PRIVACY EMAIL] or write to [POSTAL ADDRESS]. This notice covers SESSION. Other services, including an identity provider you use to sign in, explain their own practices in their notices.

## Information we handle

| Information | Source and purpose | Who can receive it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account identity: [EXACT FIELDS RECEIVED], internal member ID, eligibility information and records of any permissions or choices you provide | You and the sign-in provider; create an account, authenticate requests, and record your choices | SESSION's authorized personnel and providers supporting these functions |
| Profile: display name, role, avatar, biography and any other profile fields you choose | You; identify yourself and find collaborators | The audience selected for the profile; room members may see your display identity even if your discovery profile is private |
| Audio and project information: uploaded recordings, stems, titles, tags, tempo/key information, working versions, notes, credits, and permissions | You and collaborators; store, play, develop, and share projects as requested | You, the members you authorize, and public listeners or collaborators when you choose that setting; storage and delivery providers |
| Room information: membership, timestamps, text messages, and connection/signaling records | Room activity; connect members, deliver chat, maintain room state, and investigate connection or safety issues | Room participants and the providers and authorized personnel needed to operate or support the room |
| Live audio/video | Your device when you enable it; send your performance or conversation to participants | Other participants; connection services as explained below |
| Technical records: network address, request time, browser/device information, security events, and errors to the extent generated by the hosting stack | Your device and service infrastructure; operate, secure, troubleshoot, and prevent misuse | Hosting/security providers and authorized personnel |
| Requests and reports: contact details, relevant messages or files, verification information, complaint and response records | You, reporters, or parties involved; respond to requests, resolve complaints, meet legal duties | Personnel and providers handling the matter; affected parties where needed, including the copyright forwarding process |

Please keep unnecessary sensitive information out of profiles, filenames, chat, and recordings. A voice, image, or lyric can itself contain personal information. We do not ask for your identity-provider password.

## Visibility and live rooms

Private projects are limited through SESSION to their owner and people the owner authorizes. Sharing with a room grants the access described beside that control; it does not make the source public. Public audio and public profile fields can be viewed by the audience described at publication, and recipients may make copies outside SESSION. Making an item private later cannot retrieve those copies.

Live media uses browser WebRTC connections. Cloudflare STUN helps devices establish direct connections. The connection service receives network information needed for setup, and direct connections may reveal your public network address to other participants. Cloudflare TURN is configured to support connections that need a relay. When used, it relays media packets and processes network and connection information, using temporary access credentials issued through SESSION. Connection quality and availability vary by network.

SESSION does not record live room audio or video in the initial release. Room text chat and connection-signaling data are stored separately. Live transport protections do not make stored projects or chat end-to-end encrypted. We cannot prevent a participant from making an outside recording. Browser camera and microphone permissions and the room's device controls let you control future capture and transmission.

## How we use and disclose information

We use information to provide the features you request, honor sharing settings, maintain accounts, protect the service, provide support, address reports, and meet legal obligations. We may examine relevant stored information when necessary for a specific support, security, legal, or abuse matter. Access is restricted to people who need it for that task; private projects are not routinely made available to other members or reviewed for unrelated purposes.

Our infrastructure includes Cloudflare hosting/storage/database services and [IDENTITY SERVICE OPERATOR]. The live connection services are described above. We may also use [SUPPORT AND SECURITY PROVIDERS]. Providers receive information necessary for their role and are subject to appropriate contractual and access restrictions where they act on our behalf.

We disclose information when you direct us to share it, when reasonably necessary to comply with applicable law or a valid legal process, to protect rights and safety, or to handle a dispute. We assess requests and disclose only what is appropriate for the purpose. If the business is reorganized, acquired, or transferred, relevant information may be disclosed with appropriate protections, and a successor must address applicable privacy commitments and notice obligations.

The initial service does not sell personal information, share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, run targeted advertising, or use member content to train general-purpose AI models. We do not send promotional messages without the choice required by applicable law.

## Cookies, local storage, and tracking choices

Browser arrangement recovery is on by default for signed-in members on each browser. The local database, session-arrangement-recovery-v1, stores account-scoped project titles, musical arrangements, source-audio references, original saved-version information, timestamps, recovery preferences, and deletion markers. It does not store audio files, camera or microphone streams, or recording takes waiting to be added. Up to 20 readable arrangement copies per account remain on that browser until the relevant copy is saved or deleted, recovery is turned off, or browser storage is cleared. Signing out does not erase them. Recovery preferences and deletion markers remain until browser storage is cleared. These copies are not encrypted by SESSION and may be accessible to someone with access to the same browser. Review or delete copies, remove damaged entries, or turn recovery off in My projects → Browser recovery. Browser cleanup, private-window closure, quota limits, or a crash before a write completes can prevent recovery. Reopening a shared-project draft requires current editing access; recovery does not automatically publish or save changes to the shared project.

We use [COOKIES AND LOCAL STORAGE: NAMES AND FUNCTIONS] for sign-in, security, and preferences. Storage providers and durations: [PROVIDERS AND DURATIONS]. Browser controls may let you remove or block storage, which may affect sign-in or saved settings.

The initial service does not use advertising trackers or track your activity across unrelated websites for advertising. Third-party collection across websites: [THIRD-PARTY TRACKING DISCLOSURE]. We do not change our practices in response to legacy Do Not Track signals because this cross-site advertising tracking is not part of the service. Where applicable law requires us to honor a recognized opt-out preference signal, including Global Privacy Control, we do so. A general statement about Do Not Track does not replace applicable opt-out obligations.

## Retention and deletion

To prevent duplicate first saves after an interrupted connection, SESSION keeps a small server record containing your account ID, a random save reference, the project ID, a one-way fingerprint of the submitted arrangement and save choice, the original revision, and creation/deletion times. This record contains no separate audio file or arrangement copy. It remains after project deletion so an old retry cannot recreate that project; a retention limit and broader privacy-request handling remain to be finalized. Your account JSON export includes the reference, project, revision and timestamps. Browser recovery also keeps the pending save reference and original submitted arrangement until the first save is confirmed or the local copy is removed.

We retain information for the purposes described here, considering account activity, your choices, legal obligations, security needs, and disputes. The retention schedule is set out below. A documented legal hold or other legally permitted exception can require longer retention; retained information is restricted to that purpose.

| Category | Retention rule |
| --- | --- |
| Active account/profile and projects | While active, with broader privacy-request handling and retention governed by [ACCOUNT AND PROJECT RETENTION PERIOD / CRITERIA] |
| Uploaded files | Until you erase the upload or another removal basis applies; erasure removes the hosted file and its references across hosted projects |
| Room chat and membership records | [PERIOD AFTER LAST ROOM ACTIVITY OR CLOSURE]; privacy requests through [PRIVACY CONTACT] |
| Connection/signaling records | [RETENTION PERIOD] for connection setup records, including offers, answers, and connection candidates |
| Technical/security logs | [PERIOD], with a documented extension only for a specific incident or legal need |
| Support, rights reports, and appeals | [PERIOD AFTER RESOLUTION] or an applicable legal obligation, with restricted access |
| Acceptance and permission evidence | [PERIOD AND JUSTIFICATION], retaining only what is needed to establish applicable terms/permissions |
| Server backups and recovery copies | [MAXIMUM PERIOD]; any retained recovery copies are subject to [ACCESS AND RESTORATION SAFEGUARDS] |
| Existing collaborator working versions | Subject to applicable permissions, privacy law, rights decisions, and [PROJECT RETENTION PERIOD / CRITERIA]; links to an explicitly erased source upload are removed |

Account deletion has not yet been implemented. The file-erasure control does not remove your profile, all messages, or unrelated project records. Your name, contributions, or messages may remain in another member's conversation or project where a lawful reason supports retention. Broader privacy requests require separate handling; the designated contact will be [PRIVACY EMAIL]. A collaborator's continued permission is not an automatic exception to a statutory deletion right.

We cannot directly delete copies another person has saved outside our systems. We will take any reasonable notification or downstream-deletion steps required by applicable law. SESSION's data controls do not delete your separate identity-provider account.

## Your requests and choices

You can edit supported profile fields, change future visibility, leave rooms, and revoke camera or microphone permission. While signed in, you can export account data as JSON and view or permanently erase your own uploaded files. The account JSON export is not an audio-file backup or, by itself, a complete response to every statutory access request. File erasure removes the hosted upload and its references across hosted projects, including projects in which it was shared. Downloaded copies cannot be recalled. Deleting a track listing separately removes the listing, not the underlying uploaded file.

These controls do not delete your account or every record connected with it. For broader access, correction, deletion, or review requests, the designated channels will be [PRIVACY EMAIL] and [REQUEST FORM URL]. Particular statutory rights and exceptions depend on applicable law.

Where applicable, rights may include access/knowledge, correction, deletion, portability, objection or opt-out from certain processing, limits on sensitive-information use, and an appeal. We do not penalize you for exercising a protected privacy right. If a request is declined, we explain the reason and any applicable appeal method at [APPEAL METHOD]. You may also contact the appropriate regulator.

We may verify a request using your signed-in account or proportionate information that matches our records. Do not send government identification unless we specifically explain why it is necessary and how to submit it securely. An authorized agent may submit a request with appropriate evidence of authority; we may also verify the member where permitted. We respond within the time required by applicable law and explain any lawful extension.

For California residents, applicable rights can include knowing the categories and specific pieces collected, their sources and purposes, recipient categories, deletion, correction, and the sale/sharing and sensitive-information choices described above. These rights apply as provided by law. California-specific notice at collection and prior-12-month disclosures: [CALIFORNIA SUPPLEMENT, IF APPLICABLE].

## Security, location, and age

We use technical and organizational measures appropriate to the service, including access restrictions for private files. No system can guarantee absolute security. Report a suspected issue to [SECURITY OR SUPPORT EMAIL].

The service is initially intended for US residents aged 18 or older. Infrastructure providers may process information in [PROCESSING COUNTRIES / REGIONS]. We do not represent that data stays exclusively in the United States unless the actual configuration and provider commitments establish that. Before expanding to other jurisdictions, we will address applicable notices, safeguards, and legal requirements.

People under 18 may not create accounts. If you believe we have collected a child's information, contact [PRIVACY EMAIL]. We will investigate and take the steps required by applicable law, including deletion where appropriate. An adult-only rule does not replace obligations that arise if we learn that a child is using the service.

## Notice changes and contact

We post the effective date and notify members of material changes through the service or an available account contact. We obtain additional agreement where required before materially changing the use of information already collected. Contact [PRIVACY EMAIL] or [POSTAL ADDRESS] with questions or requests. For an accessible format of this notice, use [ACCESSIBILITY EMAIL].

---

title: Copyright
text:
# Copyright, notices, and repeat infringement — draft

Effective: [EFFECTIVE DATE]

SESSION respects copyright and expects members to do the same. Send copyright concerns to [COPYRIGHT EMAIL OR REPORT FORM]. A general report may identify material and explain the concern without making sworn assertions. For a formal US notice, provide the elements below.

**Copyright contact — pending.** [AGENT NAME], [POSTAL ADDRESS], [PHONE], [EMAIL]. These are placeholders, and designated-agent registration is unverified. SESSION does not currently claim a registered DMCA agent or statutory safe-harbor status.

## Notice of claimed infringement

A formal notice should identify:

1. Your physical or electronic signature and the authority under which you act.
2. The copyrighted work involved, or a representative list when a notice covers multiple works at one site.
3. The allegedly infringing material and information sufficient to find it, such as its SESSION URL or project/file identifier.
4. Your address, phone number, and available email address.
5. Your good-faith belief that the disputed use is not authorized by the owner, an agent, or law.
6. The accuracy of the information and, under penalty of perjury, your authority to act for the owner of the allegedly infringed exclusive right.

Consider applicable exceptions, including fair use. Do not use this process solely for an unrelated disagreement over manners, billing, or credits. An authorized representative can submit a notice for a rightsholder.

We review notices, seek missing information where appropriate, and act expeditiously on sufficiently supported infringement concerns. We ordinarily notify the affected uploader when access is disabled. We may share the notice and contact details with that uploader or relevant advisers so the matter can be addressed. Avoid unnecessary private information; do not include identity documents or unrelated passwords.

## Counter-notice

If your material was removed by mistake or misidentification, a counter-notice must include your signature; the removed material and its former location; and a statement under penalty of perjury that you have a good-faith belief it was removed through mistake or misidentification. Include your name, address, and telephone number, and consent to the federal district court for your address, or, if outside the US, a district where the provider may be found, and acceptance of service from the complainant or its agent.

We forward a compliant counter-notice to the complainant. The statutory restoration interval is 10–14 business days after receipt, unless we receive notice of a filed court action seeking to restrain the disputed infringement. We explain any independent Terms basis for continued restriction. Counter-notices disclose personal details and have legal consequences; obtain independent advice if needed.

Knowingly material misrepresentations in a notice or counter-notice can create liability. The detailed US procedure is in [17 USC 512](https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap5.html#512).

## Repeat infringement and review

We terminate repeat infringers in appropriate circumstances, keep case records, and reasonably implement this policy. Review considers reliable complaints, responses, retractions, counter-notices, court orders, and evasion. Multiple duplicate reports do not automatically establish multiple infringements. Serious misconduct can justify earlier action. We accommodate qualifying standard technical measures. Send corrections or review requests to [COPYRIGHT REVIEW CONTACT].

This policy does not decide ownership, replace a court, or promise that every claim is valid. A member may seek appropriate legal remedies independently.

title: Collaboration
text:
# Collaboration Permissions and Credits — draft

Effective: [EFFECTIVE DATE] · License version: [COLLABORATION LICENSE VERSION]

These rules describe the permission associated with each SESSION sharing mode. The owner choosing a mode must have authority to grant it. The rules apply only to rights that person actually controls; they do not override a publisher, label, sample-library, performer, or other rightsholder's terms.

| Mode | Permission through SESSION |
| --- | --- |
| Private | The project is accessible to its owner and specifically authorized collaborators. No permission is granted to the public. |
| Share with room | Identified room members can access the shared material for that room's private collaboration. This does not itself authorize public posting or commercial use. |
| Public — listen only | Members of the audience shown in the publish control can listen through SESSION and view the accompanying public information. No permission to remix, redistribute, release, or commercialize is granted. |
| Public — open collaboration | A signed-in member may create a private working version in SESSION and use the shared material to experiment, add contributions, and exchange that version with the original uploader and authorized members of the relevant collaboration. The grant is nonexclusive, royalty-free, and limited to those private purposes. |

**Open collaboration is not release clearance.** The grant does not authorize uploading a derivative version publicly, distributing to streaming platforms, synchronizing it to video, selling or licensing it, creating a sample pack, training a model, claiming exclusivity, or using a participant's name, voice, or likeness for endorsement. Exporting a working file, if supported, does not expand the permission; any exported copy has the same limits.

Keep the source creator's displayed credit and the source/version reference with an open-collaboration working version. Credit your own contribution accurately. Do not replace an original creator's credit with your own or imply that a person approves the finished work. A credit is recognition, not a substitute for permission.

When a source listing is made private or removed, no new open-collaboration versions may be created through that listing. Removing the listing alone does not erase its uploaded source file. If the uploader uses the separate permanent file-erasure control, the hosted file and its references across hosted projects are removed, including existing working versions that link to it. Those projects may remain without the erased source audio.

Previously authorized copies saved outside SESSION cannot be recalled through the app. Any continuing use of those copies remains limited to the private permission recorded when granted, unless a rights decision, applicable law, or separate agreement requires restriction or removal. This does not permit new recipients, public release, or commercial use. SESSION may restrict disputed source material or affected versions while a claim is handled. Privacy requests are considered separately from content-license permissions.

Members retain whatever rights arise in their contributions under applicable law and their agreements. These rules do not settle whether a contribution creates joint authorship, qualifies as a work made for hire, or transfers copyright. Those issues require the relevant facts and, where appropriate, a separate signed agreement. Owning a file copy does not itself convey its copyright. See the [Copyright Office's ownership provisions](https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap2.html).

## Shared project editing

The project owner can allow individual members to edit through a connected room. An editor can save arrangement changes and add audio; saved audio becomes available to authorized members of every room connected to that project. Saved changes are checked for conflicts before they replace another version. Leaving or being removed from a room, changing its attached project, or closing that room ends editing access granted through it. Access granted through another connected room may remain. Removing editing access does not undo previously accepted saves or erase their source uploads. The original uploader retains the separate file-erasure control. Saved-version history is available to the project owner.

## Before any release

Make a written record that identifies the exact work and version, the participants, and the following decisions:

- **Composition:** writers' legal names, contribution descriptions, agreed composition percentages totaling 100%, publishers or administrators, and performing-rights details where relevant.
- **Recording:** master owner or owners, their percentages totaling 100% separately, artist and performer approvals, producer/engineer fees or royalty terms, and expenses or recoupment.
- **Credits:** exact display names and wording, credit placement, and approval for names or likenesses used in promotion.
- **Clearances:** every outside recording, composition, sample, loop, artwork, and performance; evidence that the planned use and sublicensing are permitted.
- **Release authority:** who approves the final version, who may distribute or license it, territories and duration, accounting and payments, changes, withdrawal/dispute procedures, and signatures.

Draft percentages in a project are proposals until the necessary parties agree. Composition and recording shares are different allocations. SESSION does not collect or pay those amounts. Use appropriate professional advice for an agreement that transfers rights or governs a commercial release. The [Copyright Office's musician guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/engage/musicians/) explains the distinction between compositions and recordings and the need to evaluate permissions.

## SESSION demonstration loops

Files explicitly labeled **SESSION demo** are original synthesized demonstration loops supplied to explore the interface. For the initial release, SESSION grants permission to listen and create private practice versions within SESSION. No commercial-release license is supplied unless a particular demo has a separate written license expressly granting it. This label does not apply to member uploads.

title: Sources
text:
# Sources and drafting basis

Primary sources reviewed September 5, 2026. They support the specific drafting choices described below, not a conclusion that SESSION complies with every applicable requirement.

- **Privacy promises and data minimization:** the FTC advises businesses to honor express and implied privacy commitments and limit unnecessary retention. This supports the requirement to verify technical behavior before publishing promises. [FTC privacy and security](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/privacy-security); [Protecting Personal Information: A Guide for Business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/protecting-personal-information-guide-business).
- **California public privacy notice:** CalOPPA describes notice content including data/recipient categories, an available review/change process, material-change notice, effective date, and relevant tracking disclosures. Its scope differs from CCPA thresholds. [California Business and Professions Code §22575](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=22575.).
- **California requests:** CCPA rights and duties depend on statutory coverage; a small business should assess applicability rather than assume it. The AG overview describes rights, verification, exceptions, and request handling. [California AG CCPA overview](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa). The draft deliberately avoids declaring that the operator meets or falls below thresholds.
- **Children:** general-audience operators can have COPPA duties when they acquire actual knowledge of a child under 13. A terms-only adult restriction does not resolve this. FTC guidance discusses neutral age screening and handling known child data. [FTC COPPA FAQs](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions).
- **Copyright notices:** the Copyright Office explains agent designation and notice elements. Registration information must be public and registered; safe-harbor eligibility has other conditions. [Copyright Office DMCA directory and notice guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/dmca-directory/); [37 CFR §201.38](https://www.copyright.gov/title37/201/37cfr201-38.html). Confirm renewal and actual registration operationally.
- **Counter-notices and repeat infringement:** the restoration procedure and repeat-infringer/technical-measure conditions come from [17 USC §512](https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap5.html#512). The draft's human-review safeguards are proposed business procedures, not a claim that the statute mandates every listed step.
- **Music rights:** compositions and sound recordings have distinct rights; third-party uses need an appropriate license, an applicable legal exception, or another lawful basis. [Copyright Office guidance for musicians](https://www.copyright.gov/engage/musicians/). Ownership and transfers depend on law and agreements, not an app label. [17 USC §§201–204](https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap2.html).
